# 2 Samuel Chapter 17 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 187r–188r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_017_page_001.jpg, 2SA_017_page_002.jpg, 2SA_017_page_003.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue David tonight.

**2** I will come upon him while he is weary and weak of hand, and I will throw him into a panic. All the people who are with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone.

**3** Then I will bring all the people back to you. When the whole returns — it is but one man you seek — and all the people will be at peace."

**4** The plan was right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.

**5** Then Absalom said, "Call also Hushai the Archite, and let us hear what he has to say."

**6** When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "Ahithophel has spoken thus. Shall we follow his plan? If not, speak up."

**7** Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good this time."

**8** Hushai continued, "You know your father and his men — that they are mighty warriors and fierce of soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Your father is a man of war; he will not spend the night with the troops.

**9** Even now he has hidden himself in one of the pits or in some other place. And when some of your men fall in the first attack, whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!'

**10** Then even the valiant man whose heart is like the heart of a lion will utterly melt with fear. For all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and those who are with him are men of valor.

**11** Therefore I counsel that all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as countless as the sand by the sea, and that you yourself go forth into battle.

**12** Then we shall come upon him in whatever place he is found, and we shall settle on him as the dew falls upon the ground. Of him and all the men with him, not one shall be left alive.

**13** And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel shall bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it into the valley, until not even a pebble is found there."

**14** And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, so that the LORD might bring disaster upon Absalom.

**15** Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "Thus and so Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and so I counseled.

**16** Now send quickly and tell David, 'Do not lodge tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means cross over, lest the king and all the people with him be swallowed up.'"

**17** Jonathan and Ahimaaz were stationed at En-rogel. A maidservant would go and bring them word, and they would go and tell King David, for they could not risk being seen entering the city.

**18** But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them departed quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.

**19** The woman took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered crushed grain upon it, so that nothing was known.

**20** When Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house, they said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman said to them, "They have crossed over the brook of water." They searched but could not find them, and returned to Jerusalem.

**21** After they had gone, the two came up out of the well, and went and told King David, "Arise, and cross over the water quickly, for Ahithophel has counseled such and such against you."

**22** Then David arose, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By the light of morning, not one of them had failed to cross the Jordan.

**23** When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey and went home to his own city. He set his house in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the tomb of his father.

**24** David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

**25** Now Absalom had set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

**26** And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.

**27** When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Machir the son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim

**28** brought beds and basins and earthen vessels, wheat and barley, flour and parched grain, beans and lentils,

**29** honey and curds and sheep and cheese from the herd for David and the people who were with him to eat. For they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the narrative structure: Ahithophel's counsel (vv.1–4), Hushai's counter-counsel (vv.5–14), the espionage relay through the priests (vv.15–22), Ahithophel's suicide (v.23), and the provisions at Mahanaim (vv.24–29). The theological crux of v.14 — YHWH's sovereignty over political counsel — is faithfully rendered by all three. The chief disagreements concern register (how colloquial Hushai's rhetoric should sound) and the rendering of several rare terms.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "weak of hand" vs. "demoralized"
- **EMET:** "slack of-hands [repheh yadayim]"
- **LOGOS:** "weak of hand"
- **PNEUMA:** "exhausted and demoralized"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "weary and weak of hand." The Hebrew *repheh yadayim* is an idiom for discouragement/weakness. LOGOS preserves the body-part imagery faithfully. PNEUMA's "demoralized" interprets correctly but loses the Hebrew idiom.

---

### V.8 — "fierce of soul" vs. "dangerous"
- **EMET:** "bitter of-soul [marey nephesh]"
- **LOGOS:** "fierce of soul"
- **PNEUMA:** "as dangerous as a mother bear"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "fierce of soul." The Hebrew *marey nephesh* (bitter/fierce of soul) is a distinct phrase from the bear simile that follows. PNEUMA collapses the two images; LOGOS and EMET correctly preserve both.

---

### V.9 — "pits" vs. "cave or ravine"
- **EMET:** "pits [pachot]"
- **LOGOS:** "pits"
- **PNEUMA:** "cave or ravine"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "pits." The Hebrew *pachot* means pits or hollows. PNEUMA's "cave or ravine" is interpretive expansion.

---

### V.11 — "your face going" vs. "go forth into battle" vs. "march out personally"
- **EMET:** "your-face [panim] going in-the-midst"
- **LOGOS:** "you yourself go into battle"
- **PNEUMA:** "march out personally at their head"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "you yourself go forth into battle." The Hebrew *u-phanekha holkhim ba-qerav* literally means "your face going in the midst/battle." LOGOS captures the sense; PNEUMA adds "at their head" which is implicit but not stated.

---

### V.13 — "pebble" vs. "stone"
- **EMET:** "pebble [tsror]"
- **LOGOS:** "pebble"
- **PNEUMA:** "single stone"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "pebble." The Hebrew *tsror* means a small stone or pebble. The hyperbole is more vivid with the smaller word.

---

### V.16 — "fords" vs. "plains" vs. "river crossings"
- **EMET:** "plains [aravot] of-the-wilderness"
- **LOGOS:** "fords of the wilderness"
- **PNEUMA:** "river crossings in the wilderness"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "fords of the wilderness." The Hebrew *aravot* can mean plains or steppes, but in context (with the command to cross the water) "fords" (LOGOS) captures the tactical meaning.

---

### V.23 — "hanged himself" vs. "strangled himself"
- **EMET:** "strangled-himself [vayyechanaq]"
- **LOGOS:** "hanged himself"
- **PNEUMA:** "hanged himself"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "hanged himself." The Hebrew *chanaq* means to strangle, but the conventional English rendering for self-strangulation by suspension is "hanged himself." Both LOGOS and PNEUMA follow this convention.

---

### V.28 — "basins" vs. "bowls"
- **EMET:** "basins [sappot]"
- **LOGOS:** "basins"
- **PNEUMA:** "bowls"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "basins." The Hebrew *sappot* refers to larger vessels; "basins" (EMET/LOGOS) is more precise than "bowls."

---

### V.29 — "curds" vs. "butter"
- **EMET:** "curds [chem'ah]"
- **LOGOS:** "curds"
- **PNEUMA:** "butter"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "curds." The Hebrew *chem'ah* refers to thickened milk/curds rather than churned butter as understood in the modern sense.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
